While nothing above and beyond standard fair for cover shooters, what's present is still rather good and enjoyable. At the moment the full price is $20 and when a sale rolls around this game is easily worth whatever it dips to during the sale.

What a surprise. I read many nay-saying reviews about this one but picked it out of the sale with all DLC for under a fiver on a whim. It was well worth it!

General tactical game mechanic is almost exactly the same as Mass Effect 2/3, slightly better actually. 2 team members to order about, picked from a roster of crew that you can customise to suit your play style, the typical classes like engineer, sniper, support etc - its by no means perfect, you can't strip out its console friendly interface roots but its generally okay. 

As with any tactical shooter as soon as your AI team mates think for themselves your like WTF are you doing? and when they are not thinking for themselves your like WTF are you doing? Dammed if they do or don't pretty much all the time, baby sit them, go here-stay there. I didn't have any huge problems with the AI other than them running into enemy fire and randomly jumping out of cover to smash a window or something. Mass Effect 2/3 covery-style system and err... 'powers' like lift, push are almost plagiaristic but acceptible given the way they are presented. Certian commands appear to be missing, such as if you would like a squad member to fall in but leave another one on a position, the command simply doesn't exist. There is no 'hold fire' and there isn't any automatic use of 'powers' option for AI, you have to think for everyone, all the time in battle.

There is a big problem with the issuing of orders, when in tactical mode you become sort of like a ghost and everything is in bullet time. You are able to issue orders to your squad but in this mode however you are still restrained by walls and barriers. So to place a mine or call a fire mission in to that critical location you have to 'move' there as a human would, like down some stairs and around the wall... you can't just move the cursor there and click go. Its definitely to do with this title being a console port and you can work around it but its very, very annoying.

Voice acting, plot, atmosphere - authentic and brilliant, its XCom but probably not as you know it. You don't really need to be a fan of the series to play this, its a bit off piste - The Xcom theme is there with some alien name drops, tech name drops and a bit of background but its heavily diluted. The plot at the end it gets a bit... erm, out of hand probably the best way to say it - still hugely enjoyable but not quite what I thought.

As I got it under a fiver in the sale with all DLC I suspect it'll be there again, next time its there I'd get it if you're looking for a pretty decent story to sink into for a bit with a few tactical elements thrown in.

[EDIT] Hanger 6 DLC
You get to play DeSilva which is a character in the main story that unfortunately isn't built in enough, but this DLC changes that. Worth it if its 'included' probably adds about 2-2.5 hours if your embracing  all the dialogue and reading all the documents as well as the missions. Some good firefights here.

I loved this game. No idea why it's getting such a low average rating.

The gameplay is sorta like Mass Effect, just with less progression steps for leveling up the classes. 
The difficulty is a very nice challenge on max, with most checkpoints quite adequately placed to not annoy you if you have to retry segments.

Story wise it is fantastic, with a great twist I will not spoil. It is not letting you affect the story too much, so that may at some point turn people off a bit, but if you get over your desire to control it, the story is awesome regardless.

Play-through length is good, for completionist and max-difficulty runs it goes long enough to feel it is worth its price, while still giving you the option to skip some parts or lower difficulty so you can speedrun the others on replay runs if you feel like it. 
Replayability is not huge but still it gives you good reason to go at it a couple more times and still enjoy it. But again, I think it's worth it even for a single play-through.

The DLC alternative campaign is a good addition as well.

I mean maybe? This is such a funny game, because it doesn't feel like an XCOM game and only shares the name and I guess aesthetic of it? It's so odd because it takes place in 1962 and has some of the aliens you know from the series, but thats really where the comparisons end. This is a third person shooter with very light control over your NPC teammates (think Mass Effect) as opposed to the turn based strategy games XCOM and XCOM 2. This game lacks the customization and depth to be called an XCOM game, but whoever finalized the name did it because they weren't confident that this game can't stand on its own. It's a shame because the game isn't awful by any means and is honestly fun for what it is, and I assume it has the rating that it does on steam because of the name. 

I don't know who the audience was for this game and I just want to know why the XCOM name? This isn't going to win over anyone from that genre, as its just completely different. The story is just the classic alien invasion and you do secret government work to save the planet, but it doesnt have the depth or control as the other two games. The main game is a third person shooter that is split up by the XCOM bunker where you walk around and do some "side missions" if you can call them that. The actual meat and potatoes is a map of the US where you can have "broadcasts" and thats just supplemental story for the random places in the country, side missions that can be used to level up you or your agents, the dispatch missions (you send your agents to on side missions if you can manage to meet the number requirement (e.g. Mission requirement 8: so your total number of agents need to equal level 8) and they receive an item, new agent, etc), and then the main missions that progress the story.

It's an okay game that wouldn't have taken the world over, but it wouldn't have been held up to such high standards either.

X-Com for Monkeys

This may be a good game for those who drool over the UFO's, conspiracy theories, alternative histories as well as those who love the 50's and the 60s (even though they weren't even born then). This is not such a great game for everyone else.

The game plays like a straight B movie, at best.

It pains me that this game used the Unreal 3 engine instead of Mafia's II Ilusion engine, even though 2K Games owns the former. The differences are apparent and Mafia II came out 3 years ago. The game's facial animations are pretty lifeless, the lip sync is nonexistent, the anti-aliasing is somewhat noticeable, there are some texture pop-ins in the background in open levels, the fire/explosion effects are bad as well. It is ridiculous to still be playing with such graphics in Q3 2013, but at least the game allows you to get a 100 FOV which makes you see a enough of your surroundings,.

The overall visuals resemble some sort of a grainy pallet, as if you are watching the game through the lens of the late 70's camera.

Walking around the Xcom base is one of the best highlights of the game, at least it seems so at first. Once you soak in the fact that most AI models are pretty much lifeless the feeling wears off pretty fast.

Unlike in the Enemy Unknown you will have opportunities to sneak up on enemies and be able to set up mini-ambushes, although your element of surprise won't last longer than 2 seconds, the enemy will always know where you are, and why shouldn't they? There is always only one approach to beating the level. The levels are linear although they do provide for some flexibility with cover. And this is the first game that I have seen (since Splinter Cell Conviction) that allows you to switch cover diagonally.

The game loads the level as you progress - each time you open a door a new portion of the level loads while your character cautiously looks around, it's pretty clever.

The game is moderately easy even on the hardest difficulty wherein your agents DO get permadeath, however you can always reload the checkpoint and start over. That kind of defeats the purpose of the Ironman feature that Enemy Uknown had. But then again, Enemy Uknown did not feature the main protagonist. Or maybe it makes little sense to compare the two games since they have been in a parallel
development for quite some time. If anything, this game's combat is closer to Mass Effect than anything. You can heal your squad in an instant, you can pull enemies out of their cover, zap the enemy's shield, set up turrets, use drones, except somehow you manage to do so in mid-twentieth century America.

The squad AI is so-so. Sometimes they are able to kill the enemy by themselves and sometimes they rush out into the battlefield and get knocked down and later bleed out if you don't rush into the hail of bullets yourself in order to try to save them - which kind of defeats the purpose of a smart squad especially when you are on the defensive - major minus. However, it does feel good when you send an enemy to outflank a turret while you get the turret's attention. Moments like that work in the Bureau's favor.

Your squad mates are sure to run out of cover into the open when they are being flushed out with the grenades. And keeping them in line by rallying them to yourself does not work in the midst of the battle. However, all of this DOES push you forward to be decisive in your actions. Should you take a little too long to outsmart and outgun the enemy you are likely to lose a squad-made.

As for the enemy AI, well, 90% of the time they expose their heads from out of cover - so sniper rifle is essential, even with its 15 bullet ammo capacity. So even on the hardest mode all you need is one head shot to kill a medium strength alien.

There are a few things that bothered me. Some of the human tech you have from the beginning is way too advanced. Stealth? Automatic Squad Heal? Smart turrets? What's cool about the X-Com games is that you always faced overwhelming odds with realistic human tech at first - it's the way of the underdog. It's the challenge that counts. And that's what I expected to get from this game.

The game did not do a good job of building up the tension. The prologue mission has you killing aliens left and right. Your character is a natural right away. Okay, he fought the Japanese and then some Vietnamese, but still...

Sure there is a story: it tries to capture the step by step alien invasion across the US and has you traveling to various hot-spots and points of interest. Recruiting new soldiers doesn't cost a thing. So you may never run out of soldiers. What's nice is the constant dialogue between you and your squadmates - helps with immersion and everything.

The game is, by all means, playable.
B for effort.

It’s hard to recommend. 3 out of 5. Only if you’re a fan of the Xcom franchise and want to check out all the games in the series. Going in with an open mind it’s not a terrible game but controls, ai and some questionable story moments bring it down a lot. The atmosphere and setting are great but basic gameplay and weak characters such as the lead counter that. If you’re a big Xcom fan maybe give it a go but lower your expectations

Not the greatest game I played, but also not bad - and definetly worth a playthrough for any XCOM fan.

Bought the game for like 2€ on sale and played through it in like 3 days.  As someone who sometimes finish to struggle games, this  one got me hooked enough to barely play anything else until it's done.

If you look at the different peaces this game is made of, none of them is really great. The voice acting is kinda meh, the 3rd person shooter aspects are okay, the story isn't necessarily a novelty in the series. But as a whole, it does manage to be enough fan service for me to really enjoy the game.

The biggest highlight was the mechanic to order around customizable squadmates - this did make it feel like you're one of the guys on the ground you usually control form bird's eye view in the other XCOM games without losing too much tactics.

[h1]Decent at a Deep Discount[/h1]
I waffled on this one. But I'm going with recommend based on getting it for less than $5 and having about an even split with pro/con. At this point in time, for a 7 year old game, I can't imagine anyone paying $20 for it. I got it as part of a $5 bundle, so it was like $0.50 for me if I split the bundle cost evenly across games. At that price it's worth a play. I don't really see a replay in my future and for someone who played through XCom1, 2, and Chimera Squad at least 3 times each that says something too. Also this game plays more like Mass Effect 2 than the other XCom games. But it's not nearly as good as ME2.

Doing a Pro/Neutral/Con list

[h2]Pros[/h2]
[list]
[*] Cool atmosphere. I just like the idea of XCom units in the early 60's.
[*] Decent story. It's an XCom story. It's not surprising, but if you like Xcom it's decent.
[*] Decent challenge. It's not a smooth progress, and while I have been frustrated, mostly from control issues, it hasn't been enough for me to want to walk away. Knowing the spawn order and spawn points in a mission makes it a lot easier so generally having to reload means you are going to get through again.
[*] Voice acting is actually fairly solid, though scripted dialog brings it down.
[/list]

[h2]Neutral[/h2]
[list]
[*] Teammate AI. A lot of people complain about this, but it's par for the course in my experience. I also think your intended to do a bit of micro with the teammates. You are supposed to be the super agent, your partners are really just support, you'll be doing 70-95% of the killing. Approached that way it's fine, they do well enough. I don't even mind so much if one runs to the same cover I am if I haven't micro'd their movement. Cover is limited, if I think it's good cover why wouldn't they?
[*] Skills. Some of them are fun, some of them are bleh. Your teammates will only use the skills they have if you tell them to.
[*] Mission layout. It's fairly linear. Which is fine.
[*] Difficulty ramp. It's predictable. Face one muton. Face 2 mutons. Face an elite muton. 
[/list]

[h2]Cons[/h2]
[list]
[*] Finicky controls. I'm playing it with a game pad and I have issues with controlling going into and out of cover like I want. It does what I want about 70% of the time.
[*] Only saving is autosaving. You can reload any of them, but you can't control a save. This can really suck if you need to leave and you don't know if it's save recently or not. That is especially true for stuff in the base since it almost never autosaves while you are in there.
[*] The earliest missions before you have skills or weapons or really have a feel for how to control things feel a lot harder than mid game. Then later you run into a few situations where you are spammed by stuff that feels like it will one shot kill you. So it's a bit of an annoying curve.
[*] There should be more early skills. Gameplay with skills vs without is very different, and it would be nice to have more of that early.
[/list]

Sure. This is not XCOM. And I think that explains some of the bad reviews. Because I agree, XCOM: Enemy Unknown is an awesome game and one of my favorites of all time. But honestly, I don't think The Bureau is doing a terrible job. If you judge it on its own merits, then you will see that it is a perfectly fine cover-based shooter with tactical elements that DOES kinda emulate how a game of XCOM would look like if the Commander was a soldier on the field and not someone giving orders from the comfort of a command centre. It is hectic sometimes, but the command HUD for your two companion soldiers is intuitive, the shooting a lot of fun and rewarding, the enemy types thematic and sometimes even scary, the story absolutely find and with an interesting plot twist towards the end. Sure, walking through the base and listening to Carter talk to various scientists and agents about stuff isnt the most fun and everything in the base kinda feels tagged on to make the game feel longer, but it is not THAT bad or tedious. And yes, the game is over within a couple of hours, but if you are an XCOM fan and you can get this game cheap, then it is totally worth a shot.

I feel the critics have been overly harsh with this game. I just finished it, having put in about 9 hours into it, I think I did the majority of the side missions too. It's definitely not Enemy Unknown, but I enjoyed it non the less.

The story was compelling, if a bit rushed in parts, and I wish they had incorporated some of the research and building aspects of Unknown but in the end I was completely happy with my purchase. The end of the game feels very rushed, and I would have liked a bit more diversity among my squad as I tended to use the same two every mission.

Definitely worth a buy though, as long as your expectations are right.

The Bureau is a great concept - I always like it when iconic series shift genres - but it's very bland and not much fun. It dares to ask the question, "What if Mass Effect were made out of cardboard?" 

If you're on the fence about this one, you're probably thinking of how cool a 1950s XCOM shooter sounds. I recommend you keep thinking about what that would be like and skip this game, as your imagined version is much more enjoyable than the actual product.

I think this is an example of a game which has poor reviews for the wrong reasons. Like many, I'd just finished playing XCOM - Enemy Unknown and was hungry for a continuation of that. While still set in the XCOM 'universe', it's a very different style of game and many of the negative reviews will be because of that, which is unfair to what is actually a pretty good game. They've made a brave attempt at making a game which isn't a guaranteed money maker, and I think they've done a pretty good job. I love it when developers don't paint by numbers.

It's a third-person shooter not dissimilar in gameplay to Mass Effect, though set in the swinging 60's (with a very 50's feel), you have 2 squadmates who you give commands to during Battle Focus (slo-mo), as you work your way through linear mission levels. Personally I'm not fussed by linear levels - I'll take them over non-linear ones which just give the illusion of choice to fill out gameplay time.

The game itself is fairly short if you just go through the main missions, though if you're a completionist doing all the side missions and exploring the base properly, and going after achievements, you'll get roughly triple the game time to about 20-25 hours.

The graphics are good, and the scenery and level design excellent. They've clearly put alot of work into quality over quantity, and I actually feel bad about not standing around too long to just look at what's been put into it, especially mid to late game. However, if your computer's falling behind on the ol' hardware department, you might find your framerate dropping noticeably in areas.

Aliens are what you would expect from an xcom game, and I found the later game to get a bit easy due to a strong compliment of abilities. Still, I enjoyed all the combat, and if you're having trouble with your agents chasing after you when you try to flank the enemy, just manually move them to cover first so they aren't in follow mode.

This game's not for everyone. Some will find the pace a bit slow, especially in the base, but honestly the game is 80% off at the time of writing this review (£2.99 ..$4.43 at current rate), which is an absolute steal for the work that's gone into it. If people reviewed the game removing both their expectations, and personal preference for what games they like, and instead based it on the quality of the game itself for its genre (which is what reviews should be based on, not personal taste), then it would be somewhere in the positives for sure.

Even though this game got a pretty rough treatment from the gaming press, I was always curious about it because the art direction and setting looked interesting. So I picked it up for a few bucks during a Steam sale and gave it a shot.

I'm not going to pretend that it's some sort of hidden gem or flawed classic, because it's not,  but it's also not anywhere near as bad as some people might have you believe. It may fail at being an XCOM game, but it's got heart. The setting and characters are interesting, the gameplay is decent enough and the game totally nails the 50-60s creepy scifi vibe it was going for.

But there are some serious problems, too. The core of the gameplay is basically console style chest-high wall shooting, so it's a bit of a shame when you enter a new area and already know there will be a fight because the area is littered with said chest-high walls. Breaks the creepy vibe, for real. What's worse, your teammates have a tendency to run into dangerous situations, and it's almost impossible to micromanage them all the time. The narrative, while interesting and entertaining for the most part, also kind of falls apart towards the end of the game.

But overall, I enjoyed the game well enough. If you loved TV series like Dark Skies and aren't too bothered with clunky combat mechanics (they're probably not even that bad, or I wouldn't have finished the game) then this game will resonate with you, I think. It's just a shame they 'had' to use the XCOM brand for it. Instead of hating it for being a failed attempt at an XCOM reboot/prequel, people might have welcomed it for its fairly unique style and setting if it tried to be its own game. But alas...

The Bureau: XCOM Declassified is an interesting hybrid between a traditional third-person shooter and a strategic game, with elements of role-playing game; but the impression is a game crippled by a troubled production.

My introduction to the XCOM series was Enemy Unknown on the PS3, so I'm a fairly recent fan and from a console perspective at that. I'm not sure how I ended up playing The Bureau, but I remember not getting very far into it whenever I first tried it. It was a decent game, but for one reason or another I never got very far in it.

Having just completed it on PC, I am a little sad that this title was so maligned on release. While I am a HUGE fan of the Enemy Unknown universe, the atmosphere in The Bureau was very much up my alley. I love conspiracy theory, X-files type stories and if they're set in the late 50's, early 60's even better. This game was essentially that. Think the style and setting of Mad Men with the sensibilities from the X-files.

However, it is not an XCOM game. Far from it, really. It's more in line with Mass Effect in terms of gameplay than anything else. It's not a compelling or very innovative game in terms of gameplay, but it more than gets the job done. I played it with a controller, and it felt very natural to play with it. 

On the one hand, I get the hate it got. On the other hand, I also am a little angry that we'll never see an extension of this game's universe. I think it could've been a compelling counterpart to the traditional XCOM universe we know and love. 

The games big twist is also pretty great. Shame few people have stuck with the game long enough to experience it!

I'm a huge fan of the X-COM franchise since the beginning and was very satisfied with the remake 2K published in 2012.

When The Bureau was announced as part of this franchise and the first pics were shown, I couldn't wait to see its release. But several things (mainly the third-person-perspective and the combat mechanism) kept me from buying it then.

But thanks to the latest summer sale I decided to buy it and all of its DLC.

Easy part first: the DLCs aren't worth it. One gives you an extra alien weapon, one gives you a short extra mission and the Hangar 6 R&D gives you a bit of a pre-story to the main game and some new - only (!) in that DLC available - weapons to fight through some simple 'survival' levels.

A bit complicated is the main game. While in many other cases I have problems with the third-person-perspective, it worked well in this game. Also the combat system is working good and most time satisfying, but way to simple to fullfill the tactical needs of an old X-COM veteran.

The graphic, the sounds and the characters really helps to create the right atmosphere for the game and also the different settings for the missions making it fun to play, even with a too much repetitive gameplay. And that gameplay is also the biggest issue of the game. You walk trhough the 'tunnel' maps knowing nothing will happen, until you come to a 'battlefield' (easily identified thanks to the huge amount of cover for your men and the aliens), where you fight some waves of enemies and then continue to the next 'battlefield'.

The only thing that keeps me playing was the story, which had some weird twist and gets very unsatisfying in the end. But for me, the game was worth money and I didn't regret it any minute to have bought it.

Like a fair number of other games today XCOM Declassified is a case of the mistaken identity.  Bureau is a great game solid 3D person action with surprisingly deep tactical elements, great visuals, and nice (for the pulp genre) story.  

The problem is the game has a lot more in common with Mass Effect than with XCom.  

Combat, squad management, agent powers, level design... everything is patterned after Mass Effect.  Even story really - loose team-building part, replace Reapers with Outsiders, replace indoctrination with infection... few more similar changes... put the whole thing on 1960s Earth = Mass Effect Deja Vu.

The bottom line, if you are looking for an XCom game - you might as well pass.  If Mass Effect streamlined for combat missions and set in 60s sounds interesting - the game is more than worth the price tag.

Note: Keep in mind the game really is tactical, on anything but the easiest difficulty expect to spend more of your time commanding the squad than pulling a trigger.

Great story! Be aware that it is not played like any other XCOM of the series. Really like playing it, even if sometimes the AI doesn't do what we want. I think it should at least be done in easy mode for the story and the universe.

You can really feel this game's troubled development and shifting direction. It can't decide if it wanted to retain some of it "Fallout/Elder Scrolls" elements it originally started as, the turn-based 60's XCOM, or a third-person cover shooter. It mashes the three concepts together in a less than satisfying way.

The result is a lot of wandering around doing nothing, listening to one-way conversations on your radio, and ridiculous conversation decisions that seem to have little, if any, impact. Other X-COM games give you a lot of control but it feels like the missions are on rails and since your agent puts their gun away during non-combat segments you lose a lot of tension.

Even at the base you have to walk to Ops, walk to the Armory, walk to Research, so on and so on. You spend more time walking doing nothing or navigating conversation trees you'll quickly stop caring about when you realize it's just a waste of time.

Actual combat is kind of "meh". By the time this game was released there were tons of 3rd person cover shooters and this doesn't even give a good XCOM style flair to the format. Pausing combat to issue orders is a gamble as well since the game will "move" slightly in between orders and you can find yourself unpausing to get blasted in the face. Poor user cues often means you don't know where the enemy is or where you are supposed to go.

In short, the game is a big mess and likely released just so they could get some of their money back from the long troubled development. Not even particularly worthwhile for die-hard XCOM fans.

I have played the XCom games since UFO Defense.  When I saw this game for PS3 I bought it, and again for PC.  It was even better on PC with the mouse and keyboard controls.

The graphics are great for this being an aging title.  The game itself feels like a third-person version of the strategy games set in the 60s.  You're still able to pick your squad mates, gear them out, and give them orders during the mission.  You still pick missions on a world map, with some missions being required for the story.  You don't develop your base, but you walk around your base, check out the different levels and labs, and can interact with the people in it and various objects.  The base is essentially your mission hub where you can recruit team members, set up your squad, and pick missions.

There are some small bugs and glitches throughout the game, but nothing game-breaking that I've encountered.  The sound is atmospheric and on par with the other XCom titles.

If you're a fan of the series, or are interested in a good 3rd person shooter, I highly recommend this game.  I honestly wish they would release a sequel, or one set in the Enemy Unknown setting.
Loved it, graphics still hold good after 13 years, loved the play style with 2 other agents, the guns, the fighting and the story was quite unique and interesting.

I was a bit wary of this game after all the poor reviews but I loved XCOM and it was on sale so I bought it and I was pleasantly surprised.
The Graphics are excellent , the voice acting is great and the game may not be a classic but it's a definate 7/10.
If you like XCOM and want to play from your soliders perspective , then you will enjoy this.
It isn't perfect but ignore the bad reviews as I personally think these are by people who didn't stick with it as it gets better each level.
It won't change your life but it will give you a few hours of good gaming.

I tried to give it a chance
I honestly did. I went into it expecting a decent game that just used X-com names, and after all, it can't be worse than X-com Enforcer, now could it?
Well, it can. Enforcer had its over the top, fast paced shooting with loads of weapons to amuse you. The Bureau has chest high walls to protect their chest high walls that you can sit behind.

I only got about 3 hours in until I just plain could not play any more. With poor controls(Very obviously a console port that they didn't care enough about to make it work for PC), and absolutely awful AI. Several times have I seen the AI just run right into the open without any cover without any prompting whatsoever, and several more times did I wonder if the AI actually follows your commands or knows what end of their gun to point at the enemy. After some experimenting I found the answers to these questions.

No, they do not know what end of their gun goes to the enemy, and they do not understand 'go sit in cover here so I can flank them' either. And speaking of flanking, you will need to do it. For the first few minutes I wondered why the aliens had titanium skulls, but then I realised a headshot and a torso shot are about the same. You get a flat damage bonus if you flank your opponent though. Good concept - but it just doesn't work with the braindead AI and clumsy controls. It isn't actually explained anywhere either, so unless you're quick to figure things out you'll blow all your ammo on an alien who is 'in cover' but still sticking most of his head and torso out for you to shoot(And deal nearly no damage because of this 'cover'), get frustrated, and quit.

The story seemed interesting enough and I did want to see what was next, but I just can't justify spending more time on it than I already have. The story just can't carry the rest of the game and I can't really care enough to play further.

Oh, and the glass physics were pretty good. It was nice to see parts of the glass shatter under fire without the whole window immediately collapsing. If only that attention to detail could have been spend on the rest of the game as well it may have been good

I've noticed that this game gets a bad rep, and is compared to Mass Effect a bit too much. The gameplay, while simple, is solid. I've only done one playthrough, and on Veteran (it was completely unbalanced until I got some gear), and I'm unsure it's worth playing again. Being a fan of the XCOM series, I thought it'd be a nice addition, and I was pleasantly surprised. Now the game seems buggy unless you run it on medium or lower, no doubt from some unpatched problem. Seeing how little attention this game's getting, I reckon it'll remain unpatched. So if you run into a problem, just lower your graphics. It is a bit like Mass Effect when it comes to gameplay, but nowhere near as in depth when it comes to the story. There's a few curve balls here and there, story wise, and the only real flaw that no one could really argue about in this game is how cinematics tend to unfold; it's very cut and dry, and sometimes isn't smooth enough to care. It's a bit like watching a B-Movie. However it's not a bad story either. All in all? If you're a fan of XCOM and want to fulfill your desires to own all the games, then it's not as bad as everyone says. 

TLDR: Could be better with the cinematics, solid gameplay for something so far off from the usual XCOM. Get it on sale only if you're a fan.

I think its underrated and probably hated by x-com purists because they suck at it, but if you get the hang of the tactical side of things in the first person perspective, its actually pretty fun. Worth the mere pennies i paid for it.

The first time I heard about this game was from the RetroAhoy video about X-COM. And I agree with him that the game feels a little half-baked: the AI squadmates aren't the greatest and there was definitely room for improvement.

However, I do think the game is enjoyable despite using the Mass Effect formula and it certainly had potential as a more action-oriented take on the X-COM formula. If they ever decide to come back to this or remake it, I'd look forward to it.

if you're into mass effect style gameplay (takes a bit too long to ramp up) and secret alien invasions (always fun esp given recent events) this is the game for you. not the greatest story at times (but not the worst) and the art is def showing its age at this point but the music and vibes are 9/10

XCom The Bureau.
I thought, yeah, several good things combined. Feel like an agent, in the 60ies, like the old Bond or other spy action films. I was excited. I also hate cover shooters, but this one is somewhat competent enough to make even me enjoy combat. Banter between the characters is spot on 60ies and cheesy.
Easy isn't easy. Difficulty settings are there for a reason. But obviously, I don't get to enjoy the game, because some nutjob dev decided to have the lowest difficulty still too high. 
The tactical stuff is great, but right now, I don't see a reason to only recruit agents with critical shot. But having to position my team, marking priotrity enemies and so on, is very well done and quite enjoyable.
The first muton made me ragequit the game. I am on the lowest difficulty, I am not going to put up with this. Recommended for others.

After playing just over an hour of this game I must say it is different and enjoyable, but and it is a big but.  It is singleplayer only!

The graphics are decent, the controls are decent, the sound is decent there is no real problem with this game.  It is good fun to play and plays nicely.  Just it has no multiplayer and no co-op.

I waited a long time for this game, when I seen it being made some years ago and it was said to feature co-op.  I purchased it eagerly wanting co-op... Played it and because Splinter Cell came out the same time I did not want to play this, because playing a game alone is no fun.

This game would benefit sooooooo much with co-op with a friend, but alone was just not for me.

This tactical, third-person shooter version of XCOM could have been successful had it not been for both technical and the lamebrained gameplay. What most will experience in the beginning of playing is that the program will invariably crash and or minimize itself arbitrarily. Not only does one have to worry about the lose of progress, but they must also endure enemies shooting through solid structures, an unintelligent A.I. system for both allies and enemies, and being rewarded little no nothing when completing missions. If 2K Games was going to attempt to pleasantly take the XCOM series into a slightly different direction, then they might have wanted to do more research and polishing before selling this misshapen by-product.

The story is standard XCOM stuff with Bioware-esque storytelling mixed in. Felt like Mass Effect 3 meets XCOM. Interpret that as you will. Nothing extraordinary is done with the characters, story, or background.

You will always deploy with up to 2 AI team members from a roster of agents with different classes. Pick what you think will mesh, and go get them killed. Why do I say this? Simply because, your team AI will repeatedly, REPEATEDLY break cover that you JUST ordered them to hide behind a mere second ago, which is SAFE, because they can't get a shot on the enemy. ...Even if it means they charge forward into their own demise. 

You're going to spend most of your time in combat babysitting your AI partners, constantly telling them where to go and use their skill sets if you don't want to have to charge through a battlefield full of plasma and laser fire to rescue good 'ol Jimmy because Jimmy thought that getting up close to shoot at a squad of aliens with a MARKSMAN SNIPER RIFLE was a FANTASTIC IDEA. Great going Jimmy! Enjoy that face full of alien lead. You Earned It.

...Rant about the horrid AI aside, the powers are neat, but felt like they needed...more options to them. Felt lacking. Both for your own power set and your squad mates power sets.

For how much I just crapped on the game, It can be fun, but don't play it on the hardest difficulty. Go for Easy to experience the story, go for Veteran for a challenge, and, if you're masochistic and think punching yourself in the groin isn't cutting it right now, go Veteran and try to get the achievement for no squad mate deaths. GOOD EFFING LUCK, YOU'RE GONNA NEED IT.

As for me, I can't recommend this game. It just doesn't hold itself up at all. The older XCOM games are worth the money. This...isn't. Get it on a sale, play on Easy, maybe you'll have a good time.
It's nothing special, but I can't deny the game was fun in a campy kinda way.

Very interesting spin on X-COM. Plays quite a bit like Mass Effect but more simpler. I wish they added more depth and options when it came to weapons and skill trees. Unfortunately backlash from its reveal turned the project into a spin-off. If they had more resources, 2K could have turned this into a more fleshed out game.

Had this game for years, played a bit on the computer but never finished it. Decided to go for it again on the Steam Deck to clear some backlog. I'm a X-COM fan and this game seems quite good for now. Nice shooting game, a bit of strategic moves that works as a bridge to the original style of X-COM. Good Game.

After sinking 30 hours into XCOM Declassified and beating the game, I can safely say STAY AWAY. The game is an unimaginitive chest-high wall simulator nothing like the tactics games I have come to know and love from the XCOM series. The main character is one of the most despisable characters I have been forced to play as. Not in a "he's a dick" sort of way, in an "I have no reason to like this guy or relate to him" way. There are virtually no decisions to make, no tech tree to speak of, and your followers range from wildly incompetent to useless in combat. The only good mission is the final one and the game is simply not worth the timesink that you need to wade through in order to get to that point.

DO NOT BUY.

The gameplay is a little weird and so is the dialogue. The graphics are quite good if you compare to the gameplay and dialogue so it creates a distance like the game is from 2013 but the controls are from 2002

A decent Third person, action game with a focus on squad based tactics and cover mechanics. The story is a bit schlocky and sometimes boring, but the action segements make up for it in general. There is an interesting twist towards the end of the game which is original and fun. Overall, it is a decent enough game and provides about 15 hours of gameplay, but hard to recommend at full price.

Generally a nice game, but having played all the other XCom games this one's story had tons of holes. If you take it for a shooter, all nice and good. Duck/run key combination sucks a lot, but you learn to cope with it.
But do not question the why's in the story:
Why do the "legacy" agents start with cooler gear than their predecesors many years later?
Why are there so many hints/memo/audi recordings to find that change nothing?
Why does Xcom forget about all the weapons they got here? In later games you had to research to have them....

The original premise of 50s-60s America besieged by aliens from another dimension had so much promise.  Then it got bastardized into this because people demanded classic XCOM and 2K decided instead of sticking to their guns or just making classic XCOM, they had to pull this sucker out of the grave, slap some sectoids in it, and call it a day.  Play if you want but don't buy the DLC.

I picked this game up on at around 4 buck sale for a 2k games weekend deal.  I can honestly say I am not disappointed one bit.  I can't believe the negative reviews this game is getting.  I love the time period that it represents; I always liked period pieces.  I have only played for 3 hours or more and can say the game mechanics are awesome.  I think people are expecting a turn based strategy game like most X-com titles, but this one is different.  It has some of those elements, but it has this combat system that you can give orders in slow motion to your team mates.  It's also from a third person perspective.  As some of the reviews have said it reminds you of Mass Effect.  It has a pretty good narrative going throughout the game, you make choices as to what you want to say just like Mass Effect.  I think what was most disappointing for the other X-com fans was it not being turn based.  If you can get away from the traditional X-com game idea you might enjoy this title.  I have not played enough of the game as of yet to determine if the story is any good.  The main character that you play is an WWII vet that joined the CIA and suffers a major loss in his life.  One of the things I would have liked to have seen is just like Mass effect, to be able to customize the main character.  You can by the way, customize your team, change their names and what they wear just like X-com.  All in all it's a great bargain title, I probably wouldn't have spent full price on it when it first came out.  

8/10
